tweets.text:
I know I can trade profitably. I know what an edge looks like. The problem is how rare the truly clear trades are. Maybe 10 per year.

Then there are about 100 "not bad, not great" bets in between. In pure EV terms, taking them is correct if sizing is perfect.

But I am human. Greed, bad sizing, the urge to gamble. Almost all of my mistakes come from allowing myself to take those middle trades.

So what's left is at best 10 trades a year and long stretches of patient waiting. Being only a trader is not enough to fill the time in between.

tweets.text:
Bitcoin Always Tops FIRST Against Gold.

But can we find a $BTC low from this correlation?

Every cycle, Bitcoin peaked before gold:

2017: gold topped 40 days later
2021: 120 days after
2025: 115 days after

The bottoms are where it gets interesting.

In 2018 and 2022, BTC hit its dollar low first. The low against gold followed 1 to 2 months later, and price never revisited those levels.

This time it's flipped.

BTC bottomed against the metal back in February, while the USD price kept sliding.

My view is that BTC/GOLD low is in.

Gold can drop more from here, but relatively, bitcoin will hold strong.

tweets.text:
A says B lies. B says C lies. C says A and B both lie. Who tells the truth?

Stop here and think about it. What's your answer?

.

.

.

At first I thought it was impossible, that there had to be several valid answers. I felt stupid for a moment and said "probably C, but it could be any of them."

Then I asked my quant, a PhD in quantum physics with a 160+ IQ and several Millennium Prizes to his name. He said: "Try inverting the question, young one."

Ohhh. Forget who tells the truth. Who is lying? In what scenario do we get one truth and two lies?

If C is honest, then A and B both lie. But if A lies, B is telling the truth. Contradiction. C is a liar.

If A is honest, then B lies, which makes C honest. But C says A lies. Contradiction again. A is a liar.

That leaves B. If B is honest, C lies and A lies too. Everything fits. 

Trading works the same way. Instead of asking "why should I take this trade?", ask "why shouldn't I? What could go wrong? Should I cut it?"

I wrote about this years ago, then stopped practicing it. It's old wisdom, and it's as relevant as ever. 

It works at home too. If your wife asks "Should we go on a trip? Should we go shopping?", reply: "Should we stay home? Should we avoid materialism?" 

Invert the question. Often. Automatically.

tweets.text:
$BTC Looking at all the previous bear market bottoms, after the first impulse you usually get a retrace of at least the .618 and often deeper. That is where we are now.

The 2018 and 2022 bottoms did take about 2 months to play out after the last leg down.

The 2020 covid crash resolved much faster but that also was a very unique situation.

Never have we seen a direct V shape without some kind of retest lower after the initial bounce. Even though zooming out might look like that, intraday/week we have had a retest every time. So this is normal.

For the sake of this example, assuming the 21st of November was the bottom (no one knows neither do I) we could also argue that this "bottoming" was already in process since June when price already hit this level. This cycle and bear market has been nothing like the others so it will be hard to take an example in that.

The point I wanted to make is that it is normal for these initial impulses to see a big drawdown. As I've seen a lot of mentions that the fact this didn't directly V shape back up and held above $62K was a case for the current low to not be valid. Even though we can see that has never been the case anyways. I agree, things look very weak relatively, but also that is normal for these situations.

In the end no one knows, maybe we get another leg down, maybe we do not. All I'm showing here is how previous major bottoms looked and that you always see a retrace that goes pretty deep.

Just for informational purposes, personally not sure what the next week(s) will bring us. Still believe anything around this region is solid high timeframe value for $BTC if you believe in it long term. Long road ahead of us though that's for sure.
